data.title: Add Device and Payload model boilerplate

data.to:
Scaffold the Django app and the two core models from PROMPT.md: Device and Payload. BOILERPLATE ONLY — the human will finish the endpoint/parsing logic themselves.

Context from PROMPT.md: Payload POSTs into a DRF endpoint. Example fields: fCnt (int), devEUI (16-char hex str), data (base64 that decodes to a hex value), rxInfo (list of gateway dicts), txInfo (dict with frequency/dr). Payload links to Device via devEUI. fCnt is used for duplicate detection, scoped per device. data decodes base64 -> hex; value 1 => passing, otherwise failing. Device tracks its latest status (passing vs failing).

Scope: new Django app registered in INSTALLED_APPS (plus rest_framework), Device + Payload models with fields/constraints/indexes, initial migration, admin registration.

Out of scope (human finishes): base64->hex decode logic, serializers, views/endpoint, token auth, tests. Leave clean seams — model fields, status choices, Device.latest_status — for the human to fill in.

Decision: models stay thin and declarative; no business logic in save() so the human can put parsing wherever they want.

data.body: Implemented in b53e589. New app app/telemetry/: shared Status TextChoices (passing/failing/unknown), Device (dev_eui unique CharField(16), latest_status defaulting to UNKNOWN, created_at/updated_at), Payload (FK device related_name=payloads CASCADE, f_cnt PositiveBigIntegerField for the 32-bit unsigned counter range, data TextField verbatim base64, decoded_hex blank default '', status, rx_info JSONField(default=list), tx_info JSONField(default=dict), received_at nullable, created_at). Meta: ordering -created_at, UniqueConstraint unique_device_f_cnt over (device, f_cnt), Index payload_device_recent_idx over (device, -created_at). Admin registers both with autocomplete + list_select_related. INSTALLED_APPS gained rest_framework and telemetry only; no authtoken, no REST_FRAMEWORK dict, no new requirements. Migration 0001_initial committed. Verified: manage.py check clean (exit 0), makemigrations --check --dry-run -> 'No changes detected' (exit 0), models import and Status.choices prints all three. Seams left for the human, commented in models.py: (1) the (device, f_cnt) constraint will reject a legitimate post-rejoin/wrap payload — fix by adding a session/epoch column or catching IntegrityError in the view; (2) no RegexValidator on dev_eui, deliberately, so no validation behaviour leaks into their ModelSerializer; (3) decoded_hex/status default to UNKNOWN so decode can land with zero migration; (4) nothing mutates Device.latest_status — view/serializer/signal/Celery is their call. views.py and tests.py left as generated. Note: the pre-existing whitespace-only diff in app/config/settings.py (two blank lines around DATABASES) rode along in this commit — unavoidable since it is in the same working-tree file; it was not reverted. The staged .lattice/ and README.md changes from the prior session were deliberately left uncommitted (used git commit with an explicit pathspec).

Cold review of b53e589 (reviewer did not write this code). Read plan, task description, PROMPT.md, the full diff, and all resulting files.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (all from app/ with the absolute venv python):
1. `manage.py check` -> 'System check identified no issues (0 silenced).', exit 0. This also clears the admin checks, so autocomplete_fields=('device',) is correctly backed by DeviceAdmin.search_fields.
2. `manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` -> 'No changes detected', exit 0 (only the benign DB-connection RuntimeWarning the plan predicted). Migration matches the models exactly.
3. Field introspection: f_cnt is PositiveBigIntegerField, db_type 'bigint' (not integer) - the 32-bit-counter trap is avoided. rx_info default is the `list` callable, tx_info the `dict` callable (no mutable literals). decoded_hex CharField(64, blank=True, default='') non-null. received_at null+blank. dev_eui CharField(16, unique=True) carries only MaxLengthValidator - no RegexValidator leak. Payload constraints/indexes/ordering are exactly as planned.
4. Migration applied for real: ran 0001_initial against an in-memory sqlite settings overlay and exercised the models. Device+Payload created from the PROMPT example payload verbatim (rxInfo list and txInfo dict round-tripped through JSONField); two different devices both accepted f_cnt=100; a second f_cnt=100 on the SAME device raised IntegrityError (per-device duplicate detection works, and it is enforced at the DB level); f_cnt=4294967295 stored intact; device.payloads ordering is recent-first, so device.payloads.first() is the latest-payload lookup.
5. Out of scope confirmed absent: `grep -n 'def save|b64|base64|def clean|REST_FRAMEWORK|authtoken|serializer' -r app/` hits only two explanatory comments in models.py. No serializers.py, no view body (views.py/tests.py are byte-for-byte startapp output), config/urls.py untouched, requirements.txt untouched (git diff HEAD~1 empty), no REST_FRAMEWORK dict, no rest_framework.authtoken. INSTALLED_APPS has exactly 'rest_framework' + 'telemetry'.
6. Auto-generated DRF ModelSerializers introspected to check for leakage: Payload gets a UniqueTogetherValidator derived from the UniqueConstraint (a bonus - the human gets a clean 400 on duplicates when `device` is a serializer field, and the model comment already tells them to catch IntegrityError for the case where they resolve the device from devEUI outside the serializer). Device's dev_eui gets only DRF's own UniqueValidator. No surprise validation behaviour was injected.
7. apps.py matches Django 6.0.7's app_template exactly (6.0's template no longer emits default_auto_field, and the global default is already BigAutoField - the migration confirms BigAutoField pks).

CAN IT SUPPORT THE REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR (PROMPT.md)? Yes, all five: duplicate detection via fCnt (per-device unique constraint), base64->hex (`data` verbatim TextField in, `decoded_hex` out, no migration needed to start writing it), passing/failing (shared Status vocabulary on both models), Device latest status (latest_status + payloads related_name + (device,-created_at) index), Payload->Device via devEUI (unique dev_eui, so get_or_create is a one-liner). The camelCase->snake_case mapping is documented in the model rather than guessed at.

FINDINGS (nothing rework-worthy):
- Minor, process only: the pre-existing uncommitted whitespace-only hunk in app/config/settings.py (two blank lines removed around DATABASES) was swept into b53e589 rather than left uncommitted as plan lines 205-206 asked. The content is preserved and unreverted (AC 10 satisfied in substance) and there is zero functional impact - it just means that cosmetic hunk is now attributed to HDT-5. Not worth a rework cycle; noting so it is a record, not a mystery. Lesson for future implementers: `git add <file>` stages sibling hunks too - use `git add -p` when a file already has someone else's in-flight change.
- Nit, no action: decoded_hex max_length=64 is an arbitrary-but-generous ceiling (the PROMPT example decodes to '01'). Fine.
- Nit, no action: PositiveBigIntegerField gives the serializer max_value 9223372036854775807 rather than a 32-bit ceiling. That is the deliberate headroom trade the plan made, not an oversight.

Acceptance criteria 1-10: all met. The boilerplate is genuinely finishable - the seams (decode, latest_status update, dev_eui format, fCnt reset/wrap) are each named in a comment that says why, and none of them requires a migration to start using. Neither over- nor under-built.

VERDICT: PASS. No inline fixes were needed; no files were changed by this review.
